title: The Blind Man's Lamp
summary: Nasruddin met a blind man walking through the dark streets at midnight, carrying a heavy earthen water jar on his shoulder and a brightly burning lantern in his hand....
full_text:
Nasruddin met a blind man walking through the dark streets at midnight, carrying a heavy earthen water jar on his shoulder and a brightly burning lantern in his hand.

Nasruddin asked: "My friend, you are blind and day and night are the same to you; why do you carry a burning lamp?"

The blind man smiled: "I carry the lamp not that I may see where I am going, but so that careless people with eyes may not bump into me and break my water jar!"

Nasruddin bowed with deep respect, realizing that the blind man saw more clearly than those with sight.
moral: True courtesy thinks of the blindness of others.
